description:
Masking behaviour of the field rules, the project mask rules, the header allowlist and image bodies. Shared vectors: the Python SDK is the source of truth and any other SDK runs the same file and must reproduce every expected value exactly. Each case is {name, op, input, expected}; op names one of the operations below. JSON bodies are source text, masked bodies are Python json.dumps text, and form and query output is urlencode(doseq=True) text; compare them as strings. A string of many equal characters is written {"$repeat": "a", "times": 65537}, and a string made of such parts {"$concat": [...]}; expand them before use.
Operations used in this file:
- compile_field_rules: input {field_rules}; expected the compiled sets as sorted lists: keep_body, keep_query, keep_header, keep_resp, keep_resp_header, keep_resp_status, mask_resp_status, keep_resp_header_status, mask_resp_header_status (the last four as [status, path] pairs sorted by status then path), and the objects body_mask_types, query_mask_types, resp_mask_types.
- apply_field_rules: input {field_rules, body, headers, query, content_type, project_defaults, salt, email_domain}; compile the field rules, then mask a request. project_defaults is null or {field_masks, regex_masks}, compiled as the project's extra rules. salt is the STUBSMITH_MASK_SALT string (null means unset). email_domain null means the default. expected {body, headers, query}, compared as exact text.
- apply_resp_field_rules: same input as apply_field_rules without query, plus resp_status (an integer or null); expected {body, headers}.
- compile_and_mask: input {field_masks, regex_masks, body, headers, query, content_type}; compile the two lists as the project's mask rules (any JSON, including malformed values), then mask_known. expected {rules: {unusable, field_masks (sorted), regex_replacements (the replacement text of each usable regex, in order)}, body, headers, query}.
- mask_all: input {body, headers, query, content_type}; expected {body, headers, query}.
- binary_placeholder: input {content_type}; expected {is_image, subtype, data_base64}: the last two are null unless the type is an image, otherwise the placeholder's canonical subtype and its bytes in base64.
Not vectorised (each stays a test in its own repository):
- tests/test_privacy_modules.py::TestCompileRules::test_i_flag_prepends_prefix: reads the Python pattern string for (?i); the behaviour is in case_insensitive_regex_flag
- tests/test_placeholders.py::TestFormatValidity::test_iban_mod97_boundary_check98: calls the private generator with crafted bytes
- tests/test_value_types.py::TestClassifyScalar::test_never_raises_on_bytes: a bytes value is not JSON
- tests/test_classifier_spec.py::TestGeneratedFromSpec and TestSpecExamples (7 tests): driven by the shared classifier spec file, not by these vectors
- tests/test_capture.py: the requests and httpx capture tests, the userinfo and free-text form tests, the prepared-request test, the streaming and stream-guard tests, and the debug-logging and refusal-warning tests: need a real HTTP exchange through the instrumented client, or log capture
- tests/test_pipeline.py::TestClientPipelineIntegration::test_pipeline_payload_enqueued_with_source_and_duration: needs a real HTTP exchange and the client queue
